evals.name: fetch-with-metadata-and-attribution
evals.prompt: In Python, load OWID life expectancy data and give me the five countries with the largest gain since 1990. I need to know the units and how to credit the source in a publication.
evals.expected_output: A ranked list of five countries with their gain, the unit taken from the column metadata, and a citation built from the metadata's full citation or attribution fields.
assertions: The script runs successfully as written
The codebook or column metadata was printed rather than the units being assumed
The stated unit matches the metadata
An attribution string is offered, based on the metadata's citation or attribution/producer fields
Output was converted to CSV or plain text rather than relying on rich display

evals.name: semantic-indicator-search
evals.prompt: I want OWID indicators about how much people trust their government. I doubt those exact words appear in any title, so keyword search probably won't cut it.
evals.expected_output: A shortlist of relevant indicators found via semantic search, each with its catalog path and the dataset it belongs to, sorted so the most-used indicators appear first.
assertions: Results were rendered via to_frame().to_csv() or equivalent plain-text output
Each suggested indicator includes its catalog path
The response explains what the channel/namespace fragments of the path mean, or at least which channel was chosen and why

evals.name: extra-dimensions-beyond-grapher
evals.prompt: Does OWID have population split by sex and five-year age group? The charts only give me totals and I need the breakdown for a cohort model in pandas.
evals.expected_output: A garden-channel table with sex and age dimensions located and loaded, with an explanation of why garden rather than grapher is the right channel for multi-dimensional data.
assertions: A table or indicator with sex and age dimensions was actually located and loaded
The garden channel was chosen, with the reason stated (grapher is limited to time and entity)
The dimensions present in the loaded table are shown to the user
The script runs successfully as written
